records.source_title: Long term observations on the alimentation of wild Eastern Greek Tortoises Testudo graeca ibera in Dobrogea, Romania
records.plant_taxon: Taraxacum officinale; Sonchus sp.; Trifolium sp.; Medicago sp.
records.supports: Wild T. g. ibera directly ingested the listed plant taxa; the study reports categorical observation frequencies.
records.does_not_support: The wild observation frequencies are not captive diet percentages, daily feeding amounts, or proof that a Korean retail plant with a broader/common name is the same taxon.

records.source_title: Notes on the diet of Testudo hermanni boettgeri and T. graeca ibera in south-western Bulgaria with first cases of geophagy and myrmecophagy from the country
records.plant_taxon: Cichorium intybus; Taraxacum sp.; Medicago sp.; Sedum rubens; Sedum album
records.plant_part_state: wild ingestion; plant-specific part/state not quantified in repository source note
records.supports: Field observations document ingestion of these taxa by wild T. graeca ibera in south-western Bulgaria.
records.does_not_support: The paper does not establish plant-specific captive feeding ratios, long-term captive dose, or that Korean Sedum sarmentosum is equivalent to the observed Sedum species.

records.source_title: Nutrition and husbandry conditions of Palearctic tortoises (Testudo spp.) in captivity
records.supports: In a survey of 1,075 keepers, a summer diet category containing at least 80% grasses/weeds was associated with lower pyramiding occurrence than diets below that category.
records.does_not_support: This observational combined category does not prove causality, does not establish safety of any individual grass species, and does not prescribe an Ibera-specific grass percentage.

records.source_title: Feeding Mediterranean Tortoises – Some Basic Guidelines for a Healthy Diet
records.plant_taxon: multiple plants including dandelion, sow-thistle, white clover, Rosa leaves/petals and romaine/red leaf lettuce
records.plant_part_state: fresh plant foods; parts as specified by source
records.supports: Specialist husbandry guidance supports a varied weed-based diet and lists these plants in differentiated feeding contexts.
records.does_not_support: The guidance does not make every listed plant a staple or unlimited food and does not establish a universal fixed feeding percentage.

records.plant_part_state: leaves and flowers; root treated separately
records.supports: The specialist plant database classifies chicory as Feed in Moderation and allows leaves and flowers as part of a varied diet.
records.does_not_support: It does not establish chicory as a staple or unlimited food; its root guidance is different and the entry is not an Ibera-specific feeding trial.
